note: Verse-attribution corrections to data/hardy-refs.json, applied by tools/parse-hardy.py after parsing so they survive a re-run. 2026-09-05: the walker was rebuilt to bound every page by its running head (a verso head names the page's first verse, a recto head its last), and it now reproduces ALL FIVE of the moves below on its own, from the page rather than from a human's reading — they are kept as no-ops because they are the evidence that the rebuilt walker agrees with what was checked by hand. Each entry records its evidence, because a correction to a scholarly apparatus must be checkable.

moves.reason: Found by the Jacob 4 adjudication pass. Jacob 4:3 is about engraving words on plates and has no contact with a vineyard or an olive tree. Jacob 5:3 is 'I will liken thee, O House of Israel, like unto a tame olive tree, which a man took and nourished in his vineyard' — which is what Isaiah 5:1-7 (the vineyard song), Luke 13:6-9 (the barren fig tree in a vineyard) and Romans 11:17-24 (the olive tree) are cross-references to. A one-chapter slip; Hardy's neighbouring rows at 4:16 and 4:17 are correctly placed, so this is not a systematic offset.

Found by the Jacob 5 pass, corrected by tools/audit-hardy.py. Jacob 5:4 is the master pruning a decaying tree; it has no hand in it. Both Jacob 5:47 ('I have stretched forth mine hand almost all the day long') and Jacob 6:4 ('he stretches forth his hands unto them all the day long … a stiffnecked and a gainsaying people') use the sentence, and the row was first moved to 5:47 on the Jacob 5 agent's evidence. 6:4 is the right home: it keeps the verse number, which is this parser's drift signature, and it alone carries 'gainsaying', the second of Romans 10:21's two KJV singletons. Isaiah 65:2 reads 'spread out my hands … rebellious people' and supplies neither.

Found by the Jacob 5 pass. Jacob 5:2 is the bare summons 'Hearken O ye House of Israel'. Jacob 6:2 reads 'in the day that he shall set his hand again the second time to recover his people', which is Isaiah 11:11's 'the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people' almost verbatim. A one-chapter slip, the same shape as Jacob 4:3 → 5:3.

Found by tools/audit-hardy.py's chapter-shift test. Jacob 5:6 is about young and tender branches. Jacob 6:6 reads 'Yea, to-day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts', which is Psalm 95:7-8 almost verbatim. Verse number preserved, chapter one early — the same signature as 4:3→5:3 and 5:2→6:2.

Found by tools/audit-hardy.py. Hardy keys each verse of the transcribed Isaiah blocks to its source (20:3→Isa 48:3, 20:6→48:6, 20:10→48:10, 21:7→49:7, 21:20→49:20, 21:24→49:24), so 1 Nephi 20 answers to Isaiah 48 and 21 to Isaiah 49. A row reading '21:16 → Isaiah 48:16' breaks that pattern; 1 Nephi 20:16 reproduces Isaiah 48:16 nearly word for word. This is the FIRST drift found in 1 Nephi, and it corrects my statement in the Jacob commit that 1 Nephi showed none — that was said of rows checked one at a time during adjudication, which is not an audit.

Found by tools/audit-hardy.py's chapter-shift test on 3 Nephi (keyed here scores 0.00 word-overlap, 25:2 scores 0.82). Page 509 carries three footnotes keyed '2': 'a 2 ATV Sun of righteousness (= Mal 4.2); cf. 2 Ne 26.9; Ether 9.22', 'b 2 P calves of the stall (= Mal 4.2); cf. 1 Ne 22.24', both on 25:2 ('unto you that fear my name, shall the Son of Righteousness arise with healing in his wings'); and 'c 2 The phrases from Mal 4.1-2 that appear in the small plates...', which is 26:2's own note ('These scriptures... the Father commanded that I should give unto you') and correctly stays there. The walker's fn_chapter picker takes max(cands) with no footnote before it to anchor last_fn, so the page's first '2' note lands on the later of the two candidate chapters instead of the earlier — the same failure shape as the Jacob rows above, but triggered by a same-page chapter turnover rather than a wrong page bound. Malachi 4:1-2 (footnote c) is left at 26:2, where it belongs.

Found by tools/audit-hardy.py's chapter-shift test (keyed here scores 0.00 word-overlap, 6:1 scores 0.40). Footnote 'a 1' reads 'That is, actions in keeping with their worthiness; cf. Mt 3.8; Alma 5.36; 9.30' and appears on the same printed page as chapter 7's own opening ('7 And now I, Moroni, write a few of the words...'), so the walker's fn_chapter picker took the later of the two candidate chapters for the ambiguous marker '1' — the same same-page chapter-turnover failure as the 3 Nephi 25/26 row above. The note's own words settle it: Moroni 6:1 reads 'they were not baptized, save they brought forth fruit meet that they were worthy of it', which is Matthew 3:8's 'Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance' almost verbatim; Moroni 7:1 is an introduction to a sermon and has no fruit, worthiness, or baptism in it at all.

cite_fixes.reason: The note reads “Isa 17.7 reads ‘from Judah, even the king’” — but those are Isaiah 7:17's words (“the LORD shall bring upon thee … from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; even the king of Assyria”), and Isaiah 17:7 is about a man looking to his Maker. 2 Nephi 17 IS Isaiah 7, so a note on its verse 17 comparing the KJV of the same verse is what the apparatus is doing throughout this block. Digits transposed, in the printed note or in the text extraction; the note's own quotation settles which verse is meant. Found 2026-09-05 by tools/audit-hardy.py, which scored the keyed verse at 0.12 against the cited one.

The printed note reads 'That is, the lost tribes; see Jer 15.16; 31.8.' Jeremiah 15:16 is 'Thy words were found, and I did eat them' — no gathering, no north, no exile theme at all. Jeremiah 16:15 is 'brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north', which is exactly the lost-tribes gathering the note describes and pairs naturally with 31:8's 'from the north country'. Digits transposed (15.16 for 16.15), same class as the 2 Nephi 17:17 case above. Found by the Ether 13 adjudication pass, checked directly against text/hardy-msi-raw.txt.
